author: TEDx Talks
description: When Dr Anne-Laure Le Cunff was told she might die, her first instinct was to check her calendar. In this talk, she reveals how our desperate need for control keeps us stuck and how tiny experiments can set us free. Dr Anne-Laure Le Cunff is a neuroscientist, author, and entrepreneur who studies curiosity – both in the lab and in life. Her research at King’s College London explores how our brains seek, learn, and adapt, spanning areas from ADHD to AI and mental health. She founded Ness Labs, a science-based learning platform helping people live more experimental lives.  Her bestselling book Tiny Experiments offers a practical guide to transforming uncertainty into curiosity, creativity, and self-discovery. Through her research and writing, she bridges science and everyday life, showing how curiosity can help us loosen control, embrace change, and uncover who we truly are. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local communi
title: How tiny experiments can set you free | Anne-Laure Le Cunff | TEDxNashville

author: TEDx Talks
description: Joy is messy, overlooked, and hard but it’s the secret power behind strong communities. Jerome Moore shows why doing the “dirty job” of joy might be the most important work you’ll ever do. Jerome Moore is a bestselling author, storyteller, and explorer of communities dedicated to discovering solutions and social change. He created the award-winning podcast Deep Dish Conversations, hosts A Slice of the Community on Nashville PBS, and co-hosts The Nashville Scene Podcast. A former Peace Corps volunteer, Jerome’s global experiences inspired Explore Social Change, a platform that uses exploration and media to uplift community-driven impact and drive meaningful change worldwide.His latest PBS series, The Good in Us, debuted in June 2025, spotlighting everyday acts of service that empower, connect, and strengthen communities.  In September 2025, he premiered his first independent documentary, a powerful chronicle of Dr. Eiman Jahangir, the first Iranian-American man to travel to space. Jero
title: Why community joy is a dirty job you need to try | Jerome Moore | TEDxNashville

description:
Every relationship you have is a mirror.
How you speak to yourself, how you set boundaries, how you show up — it all gets reflected back to you. Jillian Turecki is a renowned relationship expert, NY Times bestselling author, and host of the Podcast, Jillian On Love. Fueled by an insatiable curiosity about what makes a relationship thrive, Jillian has helped millions over the last 20 years through her teachings, courses, social media, and writing to revolutionize their relationship with themselves so that they transform their romantic relationships. Jillian is sought out for her compassionate, direct, and very authentic style of coaching, teaching and writing. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

Because when we are grounded in our past, we grow into our true power. I witnessed language barriers, cultural shock, family pressures, and unconscious bias shaping people’s lives. title: Turning Struggles into Strengths & Pain  into Purpose | Razia Shaikh-Patel | TEDxTrafford

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In From Council Estate to CEO, Dianne Richardson reflects on growing up in a five-generation family in Whitehaven, Cumbria, shaped by the legacy of mining disasters, loss, and resilience. Raised on a divided council estate where identity and belonging were defined by place, she explores how environment, generational memory, and community roots quietly shape character, values, and ambition.

Through her personal journey, Dianne shows how these early influences fuelled a lifelong drive to bring people together, build consensus, and create community ultimately leading to a career she loves. The talk is a powerful reminder that ordinary beginnings can produce extraordinary leadership Once described as a social butterfly who creates a hurricane Dianne is passionate about connecting people and organisations. She is a Fellow of the Chartered Management Institute and holds a degree in Business Management and a Masters in Corporate Social Responsibility. She believes in the importance of regio
title: The ‘roots’ to a career I love | Dianne Richardson | TEDxTrafford

description:
Dr Erica McInnis challenges dominant Western psychological frameworks that have historically ignored, pathologised, or harmed African and Black communities. She calls for a conscious shift toward African-centred psychology one that honours culture, collective identity, spirituality, and lived experience.

The talk is a powerful invitation to decolonise the mind, reclaim psychological agency, and embrace healing approaches rooted in African wisdom, dignity, and self-definition. Dr Erica McInnis is a Chartered and Consultant Clinical Psychologist born and raised in Manchester to Jamaican parents who met in Trafford in the 1960s. With over 20 years’ experience across NHS, academic, and community settings, she specialises in African-centred psychological healing and community-rooted care.

A visiting university lecturer, Dr McInnis teaches on how to embed psychological practice within cultural and community contexts. In 2025, she addressed the psychological legacy of enslavement at an int
title: African Psychology :Going Beyond the Psychology that Enslaved Us | Dr Erica McInnis | TEDxTrafford

In Reclaiming the Narrative: The Power of Story to Redefine a Community, Aboubacarr Bah explores how stories shape identity, influence perception, and determine whose voices are valued. Drawing on lived experience, he reflects on how communities are often defined by deficit-based narratives that overlook resilience, talent, and potential.

He argues that reclaiming the power of storytelling is essential to challenging stereotypes and reshaping how communities are seen both from the outside and within. Through personal reflection and social insight, the talk highlights how authentic stories can disrupt limiting labels, restore dignity, and create new possibilities for individuals and communities alike.

The talk ultimately calls for a shift in perspective: from narratives imposed on communities to stories told by them unlocking agency, pride, and collective resilience. Baka Bah is a film producer who leverages cinema as a means to shift perceptions and open hearts. A second-year film s
title: The power of story to redefine a community | Aboubacarr Bah | TEDxTrafford

description:
In 2018, Khafsa Othman arrived in Zanzibar with a single suitcase and a heart split between hope and "total paralyzing panic". The future she saw wasn't an open horizon—it was "a wall". Today, she is a branch manager, an MBA graduate, a mentor, and a Mandela Washington Fellow of 2025. This is not a talk about a CV; it's the story of how she turned that terrifying wall into her personal horizon. Her journey wasn't about one big success, but a "daily, quiet, and connected practice" built on three transformative principles.

Discover the three principles that propelled her from a network-less intern to a recognized leader. First, hear how her desperate, simple vision—"I will not fail. I will not be the same person I am today, one year from now"—fueled by her pursuing an MBA, proving to herself she "could actually do hard things". Next, learn why resilience is not being "tough like a stone" but "flexible like a palm tree", and how adapting to the quiet, thoughtful pace of “pole pole” was
title: The Power of Resilience from Zanzibar to the World  | Khafsa Mohammed | TEDxZanzibar

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the answer to your deepest emotional pain isn't in a prescription, but in a paintbrush, a song, or a sketch? The speaker asks how many of us have carried heartbreak and burnout while "still kept smiling and showing up like everything was okay", feeling disconnected and "hollow inside". Nyanzula Nangale shares her own journey through a year of internal turmoil where nothing could ease her sorrows until a forgotten childhood drawing certificate led her to paint again in adulthood. She found that only art "spoke my soul's language". This realization spurred her to pursue studies in mental health, where she learned that art connects, inspires, and empowers those recovering from mental health conditions. With 7 million people in Tanzania alone living with mental health disorders, and 85% of Africans needing mental health care never receiving it, this revelation is vital.

She highlights this as Sanaa ni Dawa—Swahili for 'art is medicine'. She is helping the community deal with ment
title: Sanaa ni Dawa: Healing through Art and Expressive Therapy | Nyanzula Nangale | TEDxZanzibar

description: Jacqueline Lawrence when she was just 15 years old in a remote village in Mbeya the southern of Tanzanian, the speaker wrote a letter to the president about an impassable road, and its publication created a "momentum" that eventually led to the road being fixed. This experience taught her the incredible power of media. Today, she runs a media house, Highlands FM radio, that makes invisible stories visible, sharing community needs with organizations to create impactful change. She argues that media is not just an accessory for entertainment; it is the fundamental infrastructure for development. The most developed cities are the most connected. She points to a 14th-century African example: King Mansa Musa, whose use of messengers and scrolls to announce his pilgrimage created trade routes and transformed villages into the great cities of Gao, Timbuktu, and Cairo. Communication is so critical that failed policies are often "communication failure[s]" because the public cannot understand t
title: How media transforms our communities | Jacqueline Lawrence | TEDxZanzibar

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Do you believe opportunities are only found "somewhere far away" or belong to people with the "right family names" and connections? The speaker, Ally Jape, used to think so, believing this mindset limited his potential. Despite graduating top of his intensive tourism training class, 15 companies never responded to his applications. He realized that success wouldn't come from waiting for validation or a title; it required breaking free from environments that "limit how much I can perform" and choosing to set his own standards.

Faced with income uncertainty as a freelancer, Ally Jape turned to a digital device that most youth  in the African continent possesses: his phone. By going online and listing his services, he built a bridge to a world of opportunities, becoming top-rated on major platforms within two years and launching the most reputable walking tour experience in Zanzibar five years later. Even when COVID hit and tourism stopped overnight, he used his phone to share his story
title: Redefining Opportunity for the Young African Generation | Ally Jape | TEDxZanzibar

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Abdulhamid Mzee , a social entrepreneur, opens with a challenge: After school, like many youths in Zanzibar, he faced the question, "What next?". He had no roadmap or clear direction, but he had a willingness to serve. Instead of waiting, he volunteered as an English teacher in 2014, a simple act that became his "eye opener". He quickly learned he didn't need a title to make an impact or be "someone important before I started doing important things". This journey of service not only earned him a Youth Leadership Honor Award in 2024, handed over by the President of Zanzibar, but also proved his core message: "Leadership does not begin when someone gives you a title. It actually begins the moment you decide to serve".

This powerful philosophy transformed the lives of others, too. He shares the stories of Maher, a young man with albinism who gained confidence and was hired by the organization he volunteered for, and Faizan Nassor, who became an employee at Pamoja Youth Initiative and no
title: The Power of Volunteering: Redefining Youth Leadership in Zanzibar | Abdulhamid Mzee | TEDxZanzibar

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this inspiring TEDx talk, Dr. Barnaby Young explores the world of controlled human infection studies, a groundbreaking approach that could transform how we prepare for and prevent future pandemics. As an infectious diseases doctor and researcher at Singapore’s National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID), Barnaby shares his journey from treating COVID-19 patients to leading Singapore’s first human infection study involving the deliberate, carefully controlled exposure of volunteers to the virus.  

Through this talk, Young explains the science, ethics, and purpose behind such studies, showing how they offer unique insights into developing next-generation vaccines, ones that could stop infections before they start. His work sheds light on how medical ethics, research innovation, and public trust come together to shape the future of global health.  Barnaby Young is an infectious disease physician at the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) and Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH
title: How human infection studies could help prevent the next pandemic | Barnaby Edward Young | TEDxNTU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Volunteering is often seen as the purest form of giving. But in a world driven by résumés, applications, and social validation, service can quietly shift from purpose to performance.

This talk examines what happens when volunteering becomes a checklist — something to be completed, displayed, and moved on from. It explores how intention, impact, and empathy can be lost when service is reduced to hours logged rather than lives changed.

Rather than discouraging volunteering, the talk invites a deeper question: why do we serve? It challenges audiences to rethink impact beyond certificates and photos, and to rediscover service as presence, commitment, and responsibility.

Because real service doesn’t end when the checklist is complete.
It begins when no one is watching. A student who’s really interested in how young people engage with volunteering and service.  She have seen how easily meaningful work turns into something we do simply for the sake of it. Through this talk, She hope to en
title: The Difference Between Service and Performance | Irene Thomas | TEDxGreenfield Youth

description:
Climate change is no longer a distant warning — it is a ticking clock. While debates continue and promises are postponed, the window for meaningful action is narrowing faster than we realize.

This talk reframes the climate crisis not as a future possibility, but as a present countdown — one defined by irreversible thresholds and time-sensitive decisions. It explores how delay, denial, and indifference have become as dangerous as emissions themselves.

Rather than relying on fear, the talk emphasizes agency. It highlights how informed choices, collective responsibility, and decisive leadership — especially from younger generations — can still influence the outcome.

Because the climate clock doesn’t pause for politics or convenience.
And what we choose to do next may decide what kind of future remains possible. Riya Gautam is an academically driven 16 year old author and orator, debater and artist. She is a born leader and a visionary changemaker and social worker, remoulding views on
title: Climate Change Has a Deadline | Riya Gautam | TEDxGreenfield Youth

In this inspiring TEDx talk, Lydia Helena Wong takes us inside the world of advanced materials and sustainable innovation. From solar cells to next-generation batteries, she demonstrates how materials of the future can drive clean energy transitions and shape a more sustainable planet.  

Wong shares breakthroughs from her research at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) that combine nanotechnology, chemistry, and environmental science to create smarter, greener materials. Starting with the transformative power of AI, she paints a beautiful picture of a collaboration between the two fields, ending with how it is a technology here to stay side-by-side, translating human creativity into action- a blend powering the future of materials.   Lydia Wong is a Professor of Materials Science and Engineering at NTU Singapore. She leads major strategic initiatives as Director of GAIN, NTU’s global industry liaison platform, and Executive Director of the Indonesia–NTU Singapore Institute of Rese

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Trends move fast. What’s fashionable today is forgotten tomorrow — often discarded, wasted, and replaced without a second thought. In a culture driven by constant novelty, we rarely pause to ask what happens after the trend fades.

This talk explores how short-lived trends — in fashion, consumption, and lifestyle — contribute to growing waste and environmental harm. It challenges the idea that value comes from what’s new, and instead asks us to rethink how speed, convenience, and social pressure shape our choices.

Rather than blaming individuals, the talk invites awareness. It highlights how mindful consumption, durability, and responsibility can turn everyday decisions into acts of sustainability — especially for younger generations growing up in a world defined by trends.

Because what we choose today doesn’t disappear tomorrow.
It stays — somewhere, with someone, and for much longer than we think. Gyana is a 12 year old author, student, guitarist, and public speaker who believes i
title: Trendy Today, Trash Tomorrow | Gyana Talwar | TEDxGreenfield Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
From a young age, society begins to tell us who we are — and more importantly, who we can become. These messages come from classrooms, families, media, and culture, slowly painting boundaries around our potential before we’ve had the chance to explore it ourselves.

This talk examines how expectations, stereotypes, and labels influence confidence, ambition, and self-belief. It explores how well-intentioned assumptions can quietly limit growth, and how young people often begin to measure their worth through standards they did not choose.

Rather than rejecting society outright, the talk invites reflection on how narratives are formed — and how they can be rewritten. Through insight and lived perspective, it highlights the power of self-awareness, encouragement, and questioning norms in unlocking untapped potential.

Because potential isn’t something we’re born knowing.
It’s something we’re taught to see — or taught to doubt. Rayashree Rajesh is a 10-year-old author, speaker, and pianis
title: The Labels That Shape Our Futures | Rayashree Rajesh | TEDxGreenfield Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this thought-provoking talk, Ritu Jain examines how language shapes identity, belonging, and the way we connect with one another in a globalized world. Through stories of multilingualism and linguistic diversity in Singapore and beyond, she reveals how the echoes of language carry our histories, emotions, and cultural memory.  

In this talk, Ritu invites us to rethink language not merely as a tool for communication, but as a bridge that unites and sometimes divides communities. Her insights show how embracing linguistic diversity can strengthen social cohesion and personal empowerment in multicultural societies. A sociolinguist by doctoral training, Dr Ritu Jain is interested in the intersection of language management and language practices. She is particularly fascinated by upstream causes such as language policies for downstream effects of language use/disuse and implications for community and individual identity, culture and tradition, and societal multilingualism.

title: What we lose when a language dies | Ritu Jain | TEDxNTU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Food labels promise health, energy, and nutrition — but not everything marketed as “good for you” truly is. In a world of bright packaging, catchy buzzwords, and misleading claims, identifying what actually nourishes us has become increasingly difficult.

This talk explores how toxic ingredients are often disguised as healthy food, hidden behind labels like “low-fat,” “natural,” or “fortified.” It breaks down how marketing, misinformation, and lack of awareness shape our eating habits — especially at a young age.

Rather than promoting fear or strict diets, the talk empowers audiences with simple ways to read labels, question claims, and make informed choices. It reframes food literacy as a life skill — one that protects not just our bodies, but our long-term well-being.

Because health doesn’t start with what we’re told to eat.
It starts with understanding what we’re actually consuming. National Public Speaking Champion
Orator
Public Speaker
Writer This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: The Hidden Toxins on Our Plates | Charnavi Marwah | TEDxGreenfield Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Bullying is often dismissed as “just kids being kids” — a phase, a joke, or an unavoidable part of growing up. But beneath this normalization lies a deeper question we rarely ask: who actually benefits from bullying?

This talk challenges the conventional narrative by shifting the focus away from victims and onto the structures that allow bullying to exist — silence, power, insecurity, and social approval. It explores how bullying is not sustained by cruelty alone, but by spectatorship, normalization, and fear of speaking up.

Rather than framing bullying as an individual flaw, the talk reframes it as a collective responsibility — one shaped by classrooms, peer groups, institutions, and online spaces. Through reflection and lived insight, it reveals how empathy, accountability, and courage can disrupt cycles of harm.

Because bullying doesn’t survive on strength.
It survives on silence.

And the moment we question who benefits from it, we begin to take its power away. Student This tal
title: When Bullying Wins, Who Really Loses? | Aarav Rahman | TEDxGreenfield Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Climate change is often presented as a problem so large that it feels untouchable — something only governments, corporations, or scientists can solve. This belief quietly convinces millions of people that their actions don’t matter.

This talk challenges that idea.

Through stories, everyday examples, and a fresh perspective, How Simple Actions Can Heal the Planet shows how small, intentional choices — made consistently — have the power to influence communities, shift mindsets, and create meaningful environmental impact. The talk reframes sustainability not as sacrifice or perfection, but as participation.

Rather than focusing on fear or blame, it highlights how awareness, responsibility, and simple behavioral changes can ripple outward — inspiring others and nudging larger systems toward change. Especially in the hands of young people, these actions become catalysts for a more conscious and sustainable future.

Healing the planet doesn’t begin with extraordinary people doing extraor
title: Saving The Planet Starts With Us | Mayra Mittal | TEDxGreenfield Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk is about the invisible limits we carry in our minds—fear, self-doubt, conditioning, and the stories we tell ourselves about what we can or cannot do. While the world often feels full of external barriers, the most powerful ones are internal. This talk explores how our thoughts shape our actions, how imagined fears can feel as real as actual threats, and how crossing this inner border can unlock confidence, growth, and freedom. It invites the audience to question their mental boundaries and realize that true change begins the moment we challenge what we believe about ourselves. Devashree Shah is an 18-year-old linguistics enthusiast with a deep love for reading and writing. Fascinated by how language shapes thought, emotion, and identity, she explores the power of words to connect people and create change. Today, she brings her curiosity and voice to the TED stage, hoping to inspire others to see language not just as a tool—but as a force. This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: The Last Border That We Must Cross Is Within Ourselves | Devashree Shah | TEDxSNK Youth

title: AI in Finance: Why Humans Still Matter | Chirag Pravinji Jain | TEDxKIIT World School Youth

description: Two years ago, the main character was just a worn out “lump of dough,” exhausted in a cycle of studying and pressure, with almost no time left to live at the right age. But three moments completely changed that person. A Tet race with a former US special forces soldier opened up the realization that they were capable of far more than they had imagined. The journey of swimming across the Red River every morning and taking part in a 5 km race on Ly Son Island revealed the power of perseverance and the joy of overcoming oneself. Meanwhile, the “100 jobs project,” especially the lesson learned from a motorcycle repairman, helped them understand that true education exists in everyday life and in ordinary people. From then on, they realized that learning does not happen only at school, but everywhere, in cold water, in each running step, and in every life story. Now, the only wish is to keep exploring, meeting new people, and growing a little more each day. [N/A] This talk was given at a TE

description:
Lyka Loriz Lisano reflects on the stories we carry beneath the surface and the truths that are often left unspoken. This talk invites us to look beyond visible wounds and listen to the strength, healing, and resilience that scars do not always reveal — What Scars Don’t Say.

 Lyka Loriz Demdam Lisano, 17, hails from the peaceful yet colorful town of Balete, Sorsogon City. A Grade 12 STEM student at Sorsogon National High School and a graduate of the Special Program in Journalism, she has spent seven years honing her craft as a student journalist—from writing editorials in Filipino to anchoring broadcasts in English on national stages.

Beyond the page, Lyka brings discipline and focus through six years of Taekwondo, channeling the same dedication into every pursuit. Creative and curious, she loves psychological thrillers, K-Pop, storytelling, and video editing. Whether leading a team, writing scripts, or exploring new challenges, she approaches everything with passion and resilience.
title: What Scars Don’t Say | Lyka Loriz Lisano | TEDxRizalStreetYouth

description: Using a near-missed sub-3-hour marathon as a metaphor, this talk explores how life is less about winning races and more about running the right one. It challenges comparison, external pressure, and obsession with outcomes, urging young people to focus on purpose, pace, and personal growth. The message is clear: success isn’t about being fastest - it’s about becoming stronger, more resilient, and truer to yourself along the way. Syed Atif Umar, Chief Analytics Officer at Meesho, brings 20+ years of data leadership across Flipkart, Nykaa, and Citibank. A patent-holding mentor and writer on leadership, he also channels his discipline and resilience through marathon running. description: Air Traffic Control is a warm, science-backed talk about using the breath as our most powerful tool for navigating everyday stress and emotional turbulence. Through relatable stories, humor, neuroscience, and a live breathing exercise, the talk reframes breathing as an inner “air traffic control system” that helps us pause, regulate our nervous system, and respond, rather than react, when life feels overwhelming. The message is simple yet profound: in moments of chaos, our breath brings us back to calm, control, and the present. Gomathy Ramanathan is an Educational Therapist and Life Skills Facilitator creating spaces to nurture growth, reflection, and emotional well-being. A mother of a teenager, she reconnects with herself through doodling and finds her freedom on long Royal Enfield rides. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Air Traffic Control  | Gomathy Ramanathan | TEDxVSA Youth

description: This talk explores how the most meaningful communities aren’t strategically designed—they’re built accidentally. Through the story of Undercity, a youth podcast that began as late-night Discord conversations, the speakers show how community forms when people follow curiosity, embrace authenticity, and show up consistently without a master plan. From dropping out of engineering to discovering hidden skills, from socks-on-mics production to viral content, the talk reframes community-building as an organic process driven by shared experiences, real conversations, and being unapologetically yourself. The message is simple: you don’t create communities: you create the conditions for them to grow. Jonathan is a Bangalore-based social media marketer who started vlogging on his mom’s phone back in 7th grade (the internet still holds a video of him failing to ride a cycle). title: How Community Building is Accidental | Jonathan Walton & Mohammed Afsal | TEDxVSA Youth

description:
In this inspiring TED Talk, Dr. Makeba Williams redefines menopause, challenging outdated perceptions and presenting it not as an end, but as a powerful new beginning. She invites the audience to break the silence surrounding this natural transition, reshape negative narratives, and unlock the immense potential that awaits during this pivotal life stage.
 Dr. Makeba Williams, an OB/GYN and certified menopause specialist, is dedicated to transforming healthcare for midlife women. As an award-winning educator and physician, she empowers women to navigate menopause with confidence and knowledge.

Dr. Williams’ mission is to empower midlife women to live their best, healthiest lives during menopause. She recognizes menopause as a life stage deserving comprehensive, personalized care and is committed to training the next generation of healthcare professionals to deliver evidence-based, culturally responsive care and shared decision-making. author: TEDx Talks
description: If you’re stuck in a sad life story, you have the power to change it. One way to do that is by asking your parents and close family members about their life stories. You may find meaningful insights and connections that will challenge your perception of your own personal narrative.  Malaka Gharib is an artist, writer and journalist. She is the author of the graphic memoirs, “I Was Their American Dream,” about growing up Filipino Egyptian American, and “It Won’t Always Be Like This,” about her summers in the Arab World. She is an editor at NPR, where she covers topics like health and finance. Previously, she worked for Nobel Peace Prize winner Malala Yousafzai, Bono’s anti-poverty charity ONE, and Al Jazeera English. She is a winner of the 2020 Arab American Book Awards, earned a Webby for her COVID comics and has won Gracie Awards for NPR editorial projects. Her comics have been published in The New Yorker, The Los Angeles Times and The Believer, and she has been profiled by The New Y
title: How to find a better version of your life story  | Malaka Gharib | TEDxNashvilleWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description: Pedro Lucas, conhecido nacionalmente como Pe Lu, trouxe ao palco do TEDx Parque Do Povo uma análise profunda sobre a vida de artistas independentes, pela ótica de um artista que viveu o grande sucesso de um produto comercial de muito sucesso e teve que se adaptar para se manter relevante em um mercado competitivo como artista independente.  Pedro Lucas, better known as Pe Lu, is a Brazilian singer who rose to national fame as a member of the highly successful band Restart from 2008 to 2015. He currently maintains a large fan base as a solo artist and also manages other artists. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: Francisco Forbes é Arquiteto e Especialista em Inovação. No Palco do TEDx Parque do Povo ele palestrou sobre o futuro das cidades com a chegada da Inteligência Artificial e como São Paulo pode ser um exemplo global de eficiência tecnológica na gestão de segurança e inovação.  Francisco Forbes (São Paulo, April 7, 1989) is an entrepreneur, executive, and investor with over 20 years of experience in technology, innovation, and urban mobility. A graduate in Architecture and Urbanism from FAAP, he began his career in communications before becoming a serial entrepreneur, co-founding companies such as Infracommerce (logistics technology), Seed Digital, ARPAC Drones, and Whoosh Brasil (micromobility). After an international stint as global investment director at Hyperloop Transportation Technologies, he was invited to preside over Prodam, the technology company of the São Paulo City Hall, with the mission of transforming public management through digital solutions and artificial intelligence
title: O Futuro das Cidades | Francisco Forbes | TEDxParque Do Povo

author: TEDx Talks
description: André Soler trouxe ao palco do TEDx uma análise profunda sobre o poder da escolha. Em seu testemunho ele conta como trocar o curso de Engenharia por Cinema abriu portas para que alcançar objetivos, principalmente através de trabalhos sociais em prol dos Direitos Humanos.  André Soler, 32, is a social impact creator and filmmaker. In 2019, he was featured on Forbes Brazil's Under 30 list and also won the Santo Dias Human Rights Award from the State of São Paulo. He is the mind behind SP Invisível, an NGO that works to bring dignity to the homeless in the city of São Paulo. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
